meta.title: Sizing tool
meta.description: Screen a Tunisian hotel for trigeneration: plant size, payback and savings as ranges, in real time.

page.title: Screen your hotel.
page.intro: Four answers, results in real time. Every number is a range, because the inputs are.

pool.label: Pool.
pool.on: Yes: adds heat demand all year
pool.off: No pool: rooms, kitchen and laundry only

price.label: Electricity price.
price.touNote: Medium-voltage tariff, hour by hour, before VAT
price.flatNote: One price for every kWh, if your contract has one
price.amountLabel: Flat price in TND per kWh, before VAT
price.invalid: Enter a price between 0 and 2 TND/kWh.

summary.heading: Your result
summary.noChiller: No chiller: hot water and pool heat only
summary.fine: Estimates before VAT. The dot marks the central case; a feasibility study confirms the numbers for your site.

results.heading: Full results
results.intro: Savings, investment, CO₂ and the hourly dashboard for this hotel, each as a favourable, central and unfavourable case.

good.title: A good fit.
good.body: The central case pays back in 6 years or less. A feasibility study turns these ranges into a quote for your site.

maybe.title: A possible fit. It needs a study.
maybe.body: The central case pays back in 6 to 10 years. Your real bills and an installer quote decide which end of the range you land on.

weak.title: A weak fit. A plant probably won't pay here.
weak.body: We would rather say so now than sell you an engine that sits idle. Trigeneration tends to pay where a hotel is large, open all year, has a heated pool or spa and is on the gas network.

results.faster: A smaller plant, {plant}, pays back faster: {years} in the central case. Both options are compared below.
results.scenarioNote: Each rail runs from 0 and is read low to high. The bright dot is the central case; the span runs between the favourable and unfavourable cases, the choices an enthusiastic installer and a sceptical reviewer would make, not statistical bounds. Money is in TND, before VAT.

payback.title: Payback
payback.description: Years to earn back the plant

savings.title: Annual savings
savings.description: Per year, after gas and maintenance
savings.demandCharge: A STEG demand-charge saving of {value} a year is counted in the favourable case only.

co2.title: CO₂ avoided
co2.description: Per year, against the grid and a gas boiler

flh.title: Full-load hours
flh.description: Engine output in a year divided by its rating. Below about 4,000 a plant rarely pays.

pes.title: Primary energy saving
pes.description: Fuel saved against buying power and burning gas separately (EU method). 10% or more counts as high-efficiency.

peak.title: Peak grid relief
peak.description: kW taken off the STEG grid at the summer peak, if the engine is running then

options.heading: Two ways in.
options.intro: The smaller plant pays back faster. Most of the value is year-round hot water and pool heat, not summer cooling, so a chiller can be added later.
options.chpOnlyNote: Electricity, hot water and pool heat, no chiller
options.bestAnyNote: A smaller engine with a small chiller
options.headline: Shown above

assumptions.intro: Every parameter the engine uses, with the value it takes in each case and where it comes from. Values marked ESTIMATE wait for a real quote or measurement.
assumptions.caption: Engine parameters by scenario
assumptions.name: Parameter
assumptions.method: How the model works: Sources and method

cta.heading: Next step.
cta.body: A feasibility study replaces our assumptions with your bills, your gas connection and an installer quote.

hourly.heading: A typical day, hour by hour.
hourly.intro: What the hotel needs each hour and what the plant supplies, for the plant above in the central case.

season.summer: In summer the hotel needs cooling more than heat. The engine runs from early morning, and its spare heat drives the absorption chiller through the hot afternoon.
season.summerNoChiller: In summer the hotel needs cooling more than heat. This plant has no absorption chiller, so its heat goes to hot water{pool, select, true { and the pool} other {}} only.
season.winter: In winter the engine runs on hot water{pool, select, true { and pool heat} other {}}: there is almost no cooling, so its heat goes to showers, kitchens{pool, select, true {, laundry and the pool} other { and laundry}}. That year-round heat is where the plant earns its keep.

caption.elec: {share} of the day’s electricity comes from the engine, the rest from the grid.{start, select, none { The engine stays off all day.} other { The engine starts at {start}:00; the grid covers the night.}} Engine and grid also power the electric chillers, so their stack can sit above the dashed demand line.
caption.heat: Recovered heat covers {share} of the day’s {pool, select, true {hot water and pool heat} other {hot water}}; gas boilers do the rest.{season, select, summer { Heat above the demand line drives the absorption chiller.} other {}}
caption.cool: The absorption chiller makes {share} of the day’s cooling; electric chillers do the rest. That is small on purpose: the plant is sized for year-round heat, not for summer peaks.
caption.coolNoChiller: This plant has no absorption chiller, so electric chillers do all the cooling. The plant is sized for year-round heat, not for summer peaks.

hourly.chartLabel: {tab}, {season}: power in kW for each hour from 00:00 to 23:00
